summary: Used the remaining run time for source verification rather than another closing handoff, and it paid off: while re-reading the snapshot path I found that one clause in my repair Fact was over-broad. It said no repair path works on a running node whose log is complete, but a leader sends a snapshot whenever it cannot fetch the follower's previous entry (replication.go 222-224), and a leader-side user restore deliberately leaves a hole above the follower's next index (raft.go 1097-1199) — so such a node can in fact be sent a snapshot that carries the configuration, and the snapshot path was wrongly excluded in general. The Fact is corrected under its existing id with an explicit narrowing premise: it now claims only that, in the restart scenarios recorded here, none of the four paths is triggered by the node's own restart, and it states the user-restore exception with both locators. I also verified while I was there that no other citation in the draft is mislocated (`restoreUserSnapshot` is in raft.go, not api.go as I had briefly mis-remembered, and the draft never cited it under the wrong file); the interpretation's reachability note now carries the same caveat. The earlier claim content, evidence and executions are unchanged and the submission validates.
